original_question: Among all trees of order n, is the adjacency spectral gap minimized by some double comet C(k, ell)?
target_in_paper: Section 16, Conjecture 19 (Jovović-Koledin-Stanić), the tree-restricted version of the Spectral Gap conjecture.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's intended extremal problem very closely: it restricts to trees of order n, asks about minimizing the spectral gap, and identifies double comets C(k,ℓ) as the conjectured minimizers. It also correctly uses the existential form 'some double comet,' which is exactly how the paper states the conjecture.
missing_details: The paper's spectral gap here is the adjacency spectral gap δ(G)=λ1(G)-λ2(G), where λ1≥λ2 are the two largest eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix A(G).
The notation C(k,ℓ) should be defined explicitly: it is the tree obtained from the path Pℓ by attaching k pendant vertices to one end and k pendant vertices to the other end.
To make the question stand-alone, the parameters k and ℓ should be quantified and tied to n via the order condition |V(C(k,ℓ))|=n, equivalently ℓ+2k=n.
The domain of n should be stated explicitly (at least n≥2, so that λ2 is defined).
The conjecture itself does not assert uniqueness of the minimizing tree; uniqueness appears only as computational evidence for small n, so it should not be baked into the question.
refined_question: For each integer n≥2, let δ(T):=λ1(A(T))−λ2(A(T)) be the adjacency spectral gap of a tree T on n vertices, where λ1(A(T))≥λ2(A(T)) are the two largest eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. If C(k,ℓ) denotes the double comet obtained from the path Pℓ by attaching k pendant vertices to each of its two endvertices (so |V(C(k,ℓ))|=ℓ+2k), is it true that among all trees T of order n, the minimum of δ(T) is attained by some double comet C(k,ℓ) with ℓ+2k=n?
justification: The draft is targeting the exact tree version of the Spectral Gap conjecture stated in Section 16, not the preceding double-kite conjecture for all connected graphs. In that section, the paper first defines the spectral gap as λ1(G)−λ2(G), then immediately specializes to trees, defines the double comet C(k,ℓ), and states Conjecture 19: among all trees of order n, the spectral gap is minimized for some double comet. The sentence after Conjecture 19 reports only computational evidence up to 20 vertices and a table of small-n minimizers, so those observations are context rather than part of the conjecture itself.
